sections.html:
Lafayette is the parish seat of Lafayette Parish, on the Vermilion River in the Acadiana region of south Louisiana. The city had 121,374 residents in 2020, and the consolidated city-parish had 241,753, up from 221,578 in 2010. The metro area counted 478,384 people. Lafayette lies about 135 miles from New Orleans, 59 miles from Baton Rouge and 75 miles from Lake Charles, so it acts as the hub for a wide stretch of Acadiana. Broussard, Carencro, Scott, Youngsville and Duson are smaller municipalities inside the parish.

Energy, health care, education, technology and retail all employ local buyers. The University of Louisiana at Lafayette has more than 18,000 students, and oil and gas work can shift quickly with the price of crude, which sometimes forces a household to sell on a short timeline. Interstates 10 and 49, U.S. 90 and U.S. 167 make commuting easy. Houses near the center of town can be old, and older houses carry their own repair lists.

sections.h2: Is flooding a concern for a Lafayette house?
sections.html:
Lafayette sits on higher ground than much of south Louisiana, and significant flooding is limited mostly to local flash flooding. That does not make every lot safe. The city has grown on both sides of the Vermilion River, and several coulees, Isaac Verot Coulee and Coulee des Poches among them, drain into it. Buyers and their insurers will check the flood zone, so look up the map for your address before you list and write down any past water on the property.

The climate is humid subtropical with rain all year, especially in summer. Heat and humidity are hard on air conditioning, roofs and attic ventilation, and a hard freeze can crack pipes. Expect buyers to ask how old the air conditioner and roof are.

The Lafayette Parish Assessor values property, and taxing bodies such as the city-parish and the school board set the rates. State law requires reassessment at least every four years, though values can change yearly with sales.

The homestead exemption covers the first $7,500 of assessed value, which equals $75,000 of market value, and it applies to the home where the owner lives. It also covers a pool, outdoor kitchen, pool house or storage building belonging to the owner, but not a second house or a commercial building on the same land.

ProgramLafayette Parish detail
Homestead exemption$7,500 of assessed value, permanent while the owner lives there

A freeze holds the assessed value, not the tax, because the millage can still change.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lafayette assessment, and when is tax due?
sections.html:
Talk to a deputy assessor first and bring evidence that the assessment is above market value. If you still disagree, you can appeal to the Lafayette Consolidated Council at hearings held in September, then to the Louisiana Tax Commission, and after that to district court within thirty days.

Property tax is due each year by December 31, and unpaid taxes become delinquent the next day. If you are selling in the second half of the year, make sure the current bill is paid or settled at closing.

A Lafayette seller fills out the Louisiana property disclosure form and hands it to the buyer by the time the buyer makes an offer, under R.S. 9:3198. You may say a fact is unknown, and the form is not a warranty. A seller is not liable for a mistake that was not willful, or for repeating a report from a public body or professional the seller reasonably trusted. A buyer who gets the form late has 72 hours to withdraw, excluding weekends and holidays. Given the water and heat issues above, fill in the roof, plumbing, air conditioning and any water history with care.

Lafayette Consolidated Government has a Property Maintenance Code, and its Compliance Division applies it to properties in the city and in the unincorporated parish. The Code Enforcement Section deals with tall grass, litter and debris, junked items and other nuisances, and the city-parish also regulates unsafe structures through its building code.

An empty inherited house can collect a notice if the grass grows or debris piles up. Clear it, or tell a cash buyer about the notice so it can be handled at closing. Ask the city-parish what applies to a damaged house, since unsafe structures fall under a separate part of the code.

sections.h2: How a Lafayette sale gets to closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, a notary or attorney orders the title search and your lender supplies a payoff. Have your deed, latest tax bill, survey and repair records ready. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and inspection. A cash buyer can often close as soon as the title is clear. Taxes, your mortgage balance and recording costs are paid from your proceeds at the signing, so ask for the settlement statement ahead of time and question any line that looks wrong.

If you have an assessed value freeze, remember that it ends on sale. A listing suits a house in good shape that can wait for financing, and a cash sale suits a house that needs work or a seller on a deadline.

faqs.q: Is Lafayette a city or a parish?
faqs.a: It is both. Since 1996 the city and parish have operated as one consolidated government, the Lafayette Consolidated Government, though five other municipalities keep their own governments.

faqs.q: What does the Lafayette homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: It covers the first $7,500 of assessed value, equal to $75,000 of market value, on the home where the owner lives. It does not cover a second house or a commercial building on the same land.

faqs.q: Does the assessed value freeze pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The freeze ends on sale, effective the last day of December of the year before the sale year, so the buyer's home is assessed at the current value.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Lafayette assessment?
faqs.a: Start with a deputy assessor and bring evidence. After that you can appeal to the Lafayette Consolidated Council in September, then to the Louisiana Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Who enforces tall grass and debris rules?
faqs.a: The Code Enforcement Section of Lafayette Consolidated Government handles tall grass, litter, junked items and similar nuisances.
